Exercise: Barbell Step Ups

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_lower_body_push

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- hamstrings
- quadriceps

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: knee injury, description: Individuals with knee injuries should avoid this exercise or modify it under professional supervision.
- condition: back pain, description: Individuals experiencing back pain may find this exercise uncomfortable and should consult a healthcare provider before attempting.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single Leg Barbell Step Ups, force: push, level: intermediate, mechanic: compound, primaryMuscles: ['quadriceps'], secondaryMuscles: ['calves', 'glutes', 'hamstrings']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Dumbbell Step Ups, equipment: dumbbells
- exercise_name: Box Jumps, equipment: box

Instructions:

- Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) and stand upright behind an elevated platform (such as the one used for spotting behind a flat bench). This is your starting position.
- Place the right foot on the elevated platform. Step on the platform by extending the hip and the knee of your right leg. Use the heel mainly to lift the rest of your body up and place the foot of the left leg on the platform as well. Breathe out as you execute the force required to come up.
- Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the left foot on the initial position.
- Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
